palette.notes: Code: 26 colours, 2 ramps with ~1 deg hue shift on a still that includes the Aseprite UI; the sprite itself is a yellow ramp to dark olive, no hue shift, dithered.

lighting: Blender lighting baked in: one key from upper right, soft falloff to dark olive; after reduction the light becomes stepped bands with dithering.
silhouette: A round yellow face with two black eyes and an open mouth; the circle stays readable at the small sprite size.

motion.timing: Code: median hold 116.7 ms (p25 50, p75 500 ms), 2.67 changes/s; mostly held tutorial steps, with the head turning a few degrees in the final 'Perfecto' loop.

texture: Pre-rendered 3D downscaled in Aseprite (nearest neighbour), colours reduced, then dithered: pixel art from 3D, smooth source shading turned into stepped bands.
camera: Screen capture of Blender then Aseprite, one step per caption, ending zoomed on the finished sprite on a checker background.

acting.enters: The 3D model appears already finished in Blender.
acting.acts: Turns to camera; its expression is the only acting. The final sprite looks up and turns.

techniques: render in 3D, then reduce sprite size in Aseprite
colour reduction to a small palette
brightness and contrast pass as finishing touch
feel: 3D render + downscale + palette cut + dither = cheap smooth-turning pixel sprite, but soft and generic
for_fred: Avoid letting 3D Fred go out as raw downscaled renders: if using create/render3d for turns, reduce to Fred's own ramp and hand-fix eyes and outline so he still reads as the same pixel character.
